title: Pollinations found its way into the terminal
summary:
A new terminal interface, refreshed generation models, clearer usage data, and a growing app catalog made Pollinations easier to use and explore.

The alpha `polli` CLI arrived with text, chat, image, audio, and video generation, plus transcription, uploads, model discovery, and script-friendly JSON output. A day later, interactive text generation gained default streaming and generated audio gained a play option. Browser developers got a quieter improvement too: CORS preflight now accepts headers sent by browser-based OpenAI SDK calls.

`kimi` moved to Kimi K2.5 with image input and a 262K-token context window; `glm` and `qwen-large` moved to GLM 5.1 and Qwen3.6 Plus. DeepSeek and MiniMax received routing changes. Veo 3.1 Fast switched from a retired preview ID to Google's GA model ID, addressing model-not-found errors.

The default Sana Sprint image model moved from 0.6B to 1.6B on a GH200 worker, which reports roughly 0.165 seconds per image versus 0.25 seconds on the previous A100 setup. Individual dimensions can now reach 768 pixels within a 512×512 total-pixel cap. Gemini image models gained an optional `reasoning` flag for text rendering and layout; it stays off unless requested.

Enter’s usage graph now follows the selected 7-, 30-, or 90-day window, with exact daily data for API-key filters and exports that respect the selected period. Usage APIs gained `days` options and stable pagination. Public model prices were separated from internal costs, with explicit prices added for Seedream and Wan. Audio generation routes also gained the access and budget checks used by other generation routes.
